name: YourGPT
tagline: A genuinely broad, no-code AI agent platform from Delta4 Infotech with strong G2 sentiment (4.7/5) and deep automation depth — undercut by a confusing credit-metered pricing model and a real discrepancy between its own pricing page and its G2 listing.
tldr: YourGPT is the flagship product of Delta4 Infotech Pvt. Ltd., an Indian company headquartered in Mohali, Punjab, founded by Rohit Joshi (CEO) and Sahil Kumar (Co-Founder & COO) — sources conflict on the founding year (2022 per one source, 2023 per another), and funding/employee count could not be independently verified beyond low-confidence estimates.

The platform supports a genuinely broad set of native channels — website widget, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Line, Email, and Twilio SMS/Voice — alongside a visual 'AI Studio' for building multi-step conversational flows with API calling and code execution.

Ecommerce and CMS integrations are confirmed and unusually complete: Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, and BigCommerce are all documented, with the Shopify integration specifically able to check live order status and initiate returns via the Shopify order API.

CRM integration is narrower than the ecommerce side — only Salesforce is a native integration; HubSpot and Zendesk are not natively supported and would need to be bridged through Zapier, Make, or Pabbly Connect, all three of which are confirmed native integrations.

There is a genuine, confirmed pricing discrepancy between YourGPT's own live pricing page (Essential $39-59/mo, Professional $79-129/mo, Advanced $349-499/mo) and its G2 listing (Essential $49, Professional $99, Advanced $399, no annual/monthly split) — and pricing is credit-metered by AI model, which at least one reviewer found genuinely confusing to track.

Independent review sentiment is strong where it's statistically meaningful (G2: 4.7/5 across 26 reviews, with the founder personally responding to support requests) and no serious complaint pattern — billing fraud, account lockouts, hostile support — was found in available public sources, unlike several other tools in this category.

faq.question: Who makes YourGPT?
faq.answer: YourGPT is the flagship product of Delta4 Infotech Pvt. Ltd., an Indian company headquartered in Mohali, Punjab, founded by Rohit Joshi (CEO) and Sahil Kumar (Co-Founder & COO). Sources conflict on the exact founding year — one places it in June 2022, another in 2023 — and this hasn't been independently resolved.

faq.question: How much does YourGPT actually cost?
faq.answer: This is genuinely unclear across sources. YourGPT's own live pricing page lists Essential at $39-59/month, Professional at $79-129/month, and Advanced at $349-499/month depending on annual vs. monthly billing. Its G2 listing, however, shows flat figures of $49, $99, and $399 with no annual/monthly distinction. We could not determine which figure is currently authoritative, so treat the vendor's own pricing page as the more likely up-to-date source and confirm directly with YourGPT before committing.

faq.question: How does YourGPT's credit-based pricing work?
faq.answer: Instead of billing per message, YourGPT meters usage in 'AI Credits' that consume at different rates depending on the underlying AI model — for example, GPT-3.5 uses credits at a 1x multiplier while GPT-4 uses a 20x multiplier. At least one independent reviewer described this system as confusing to track in practice, specifically flagging difficulty understanding how credits were being consumed relative to their actual sales volume.

faq.question: Does YourGPT integrate with Shopify and other ecommerce platforms?
faq.answer: Yes, and unusually completely — Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, and BigCommerce are all confirmed, documented integrations. The Shopify integration specifically is described by YourGPT as able to check live order and fulfillment status via the Shopify order API and initiate returns under configured policy rules, though this capability is self-reported by the vendor and we found no independent, production-verified example confirming it works end-to-end.

faq.question: Does YourGPT connect to Salesforce, HubSpot, or Zendesk?
faq.answer: Salesforce is a confirmed native integration. HubSpot and Zendesk are not natively supported — in fact, Zendesk appears on YourGPT's site only as a competitor-comparison page, not a partner integration. Connecting to either would require bridging through Zapier, Make, or Pabbly Connect, all three of which are confirmed native integrations.

faq.question: What do independent reviews say about YourGPT?
faq.answer: Where the sample size is statistically meaningful, sentiment is strong: G2 shows 4.7/5 across 26 reviews, with reviewers repeatedly praising ease of setup and highlighting that the founder, Rohit Joshi, personally responds to support requests. The most-repeated negative themes are ordinary feature-gap complaints — pricing being steep for small businesses at lower tiers, confusing AI-credit consumption, and documentation gaps — rather than any serious pattern of billing fraud, account lockouts, or hostile support, which we did not find evidence of in available public sources.

pricingBreakdown: YourGPT's pricing is genuinely harder to pin down than most competitors in this category, and that's worth taking seriously rather than glossing over. The vendor's own live pricing page shows annual-vs-monthly figures ($39-59, $79-129, $349-499 across the three self-serve tiers), while its G2 listing shows different, flat figures ($49, $99, $399) with no billing-frequency distinction at all — a real, confirmed conflict between two vendor-controlled sources, not a case of a third party misreporting. On top of that, billing is metered in 'AI Credits' that consume at different multipliers depending on which underlying AI model a conversation uses (GPT-3.5 at 1x versus GPT-4 at 20x, for example), and at least one independent reviewer described genuine difficulty understanding how their credits were being consumed relative to their actual usage. None of this points to deceptive pricing or billing fraud — no such pattern was found in available reviews — but it does mean a prospective buyer should get a direct, current quote from YourGPT rather than relying on either published price list, and should ask specifically how credit consumption is tracked and alerted before committing to a plan.

capabilities.note: This is YourGPT's clearest strength: a genuinely broad native channel list (including Discord, Line, and Twilio Voice, which many competitors skip) combined with a visual AI Studio that supports API calling and code execution — real depth for a no-code-branded tool.

All six major ecommerce/CMS platforms in our standard checklist (Shopify, WooCommerce, WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow) are confirmed, plus BigCommerce — an unusually complete list, with the Shopify integration specifically documented to reach real order data via the Shopify order API.

Worth flagging clearly: only Salesforce is a native CRM integration. A business standardized on HubSpot or Zendesk will need to bridge through Zapier, Make, or Pabbly Connect rather than getting a first-party connection.

The confirmed discrepancy between YourGPT's own pricing page and its G2 listing, combined with a credit-metering system independently described as confusing by at least one reviewer, is a real friction point that a prospective buyer should resolve directly with the vendor before committing.

Multiple independent G2 reviews, spanning different months, describe the founder (Rohit Joshi) personally responding to support requests — a genuinely strong, repeated signal of hands-on vendor engagement for a company of this size.

Ecommerce teams on Shopify, WooCommerce, or another major CMS/storefront platform wanting a genuinely complete native integration

verdict: YourGPT's feature list is genuinely more complete than its market profile might suggest — a broad native channel list that includes Discord, Line, and Twilio Voice alongside the expected WhatsApp and Messenger, an AI Studio with real API calling and code execution, and an ecommerce/CMS integration list that covers all six major platforms in our checklist plus BigCommerce, with the Shopify integration specifically reaching real order data through Shopify's own order API. Independent sentiment backs this up where the sample size is meaningful: a 4.7/5 across 26 G2 reviews, with reviewers repeatedly praising fast setup and calling out that the founder, Rohit Joshi, personally responds to support requests — a genuinely strong signal for a company this size, and notably, we found no evidence of the serious complaint patterns (billing fraud, account lockouts, hostile support) that dragged down several other tools in this category. What keeps this from a stronger overall rating is pricing, and it's worth being direct about why: we found a real, confirmed conflict between YourGPT's own live pricing page and its G2 listing that we could not resolve, and on top of that, the credit-metered billing model — where different AI models consume credits at wildly different multipliers — was independently described by at least one reviewer as genuinely hard to track relative to actual usage. Neither issue rises to the level of deception, but together they mean a prospective buyer should get a direct, current quote and a clear explanation of credit consumption before committing, rather than trusting either published price list at face value. If your priority is channel and automation breadth with a genuinely capable ecommerce integration, YourGPT is a strong, underrated option; just budget time to sort out pricing clarity directly with the vendor, and know that CRM integration beyond Salesforce will mean routing through Zapier or Make.
